# Nostalgia Meets Code: Building a Game Boy Emulator in F#

In a world where every pixel of our childhood memories can be resurrected through code, software engineer Nick Kossolapov has taken on a nostalgic journey by creating a Game Boy emulator named "Fame Boy." Using F#, a functional programming language, Kossolapov sought not just to relive his childhood experiences with the iconic handheld console but also to deepen his understanding of how computers function at their core.

## From Tetris to Fame Boy

Kossolapov’s journey into the world of emulation began with an educational endeavor. After completing the "From NAND to Tetris" course, he successfully built a CHIP-8 emulator called "Fip-8." This foundational project set the stage for his more ambitious task: emulating the Game Boy.

The development of Fame Boy is a testament to Kossolapov's commitment to learning and experimentation. He emphasizes that the project is not just about creating a functional emulator but about grasping the intricate workings of computer hardware. The emulator boasts key features like sound capabilities and compatibility across both desktop and web platforms, showcasing technical prowess and an understanding of user experience.

## Technical Innovations

At the heart of Fame Boy is a well-structured codebase that leverages the functional programming principles inherent in F#. The emulator operates using two primary arrays—a framebuffer for graphics and an audiobuffer for sound—alongside two key functions: `stepEmulator` and `getJoypadState`. 

The emulator's CPU is modeled after the real Sharp LR35902, and Kossolapov has ingeniously used discriminated unions in F# to represent various CPU instructions and states. This design choice aligns well with the functional programming paradigm, allowing for clean and manageable code.

### Challenges and Learning

Every journey has its hurdles, and Kossolapov faced several challenges during development. Implementing the Picture Processing Unit (PPU) and sound processing proved particularly tricky, requiring meticulous debugging to synchronize audio and video accurately. His dedication to performance optimization led to significant improvements in frames per second (FPS), achieved through profiling and refactoring.

Initially, Kossolapov relied on manual testing with ROMs, but he later integrated unit tests into his workflow, assisted by AI in generating test cases. This blend of traditional coding practices and modern AI tools illustrates the evolving landscape of software development.

## Web Implementation and Performance

Transitioning Fame Boy to the web using Fable and exploring WebAssembly with Blazor came with its own set of performance challenges. Despite these obstacles, Kossolapov's commitment to ensuring a responsive experience for users remained unwavering. Through rigorous performance benchmarks on both desktop and web platforms, he carefully analyzed the differences in FPS, striving to deliver an emulator that felt authentic to users.
